transcript.text: panasonic nn h98 not heating anymore, any fix?

Yes, there are fixes, but we need to narrow down whether it is a simple setting or a component failure first. On your Panasonic NN-H98, this usually points to the high-voltage heating circuit (like the magnetron or inverter board) or just being set to a low power mode by mistake. Please check that you are using full power and not a defrost or grill setting, then heat a cup of water for one minute on full power. Tell me if the water gets hot or stays cold so I can guide you to the right repair path.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
the screen says h98, not the model. model on the back is NN-CD87KSBPQ. tried a cup of water, stops after 10-15 secs with h98, water still cold

The H98 code on your NN-CD87KSBPQ suggests a fault in the high-voltage heating system, specifically the magnetron or its power supply. Since it cuts out after just 10–15 seconds with cold water, this is not an overheating issue but a failure of the inverter board to deliver power to the magnetron. The most common cause for this specific behaviour on Panasonic inverter models is a failing inverter board. You will need a qualified engineer to replace the inverter board or potentially the magnetron if the board tests fine, as these components involve high-voltage capacitors that can hold a dangerous charge even when unplugged.
